newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to sell most of state-run airline.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to sell most of state-run airline.

text.p: Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Thursday said the government planned to sell most of its stake in Lithuanian Airlines, contradicting earlier statements that only a minority would be sold.
But Vagnorius said that 51 percent of the company's capital should be Lithuanian, which would exclude idea of losing control of the airline to a foreign company.
"The government will not retain a controlling package of shares in Lithuanian Airlines," Vagnorius told Reuters in an interview.
"We would like to see private persons have control over it," Vagnorius added.
His comments are a departure from previous government statements, which said that the state planned to retain 51 percent of the shares in the country's national flag carrier.

Lithuanian Airlines is included in a list of 14 major objects in the transport, communications and energy sectors which the government has committed itself to sell through open bids over the next two years.
Neighbouring Baltic states Latvia and Estonia have already delivered their national air carriers into private hands.
Latvia's Air Baltic is 49 percent owned by foreign investors including Scandinavian Airlines while Estonian Air is majority owned by Denmark's Maersk, owned by A.P. Moeller.
